text: Your name is Mr. Otto Binder?
That's right, yeah.
Do you believe in these sources?
I believe in the extent that people have seen definite objects.
The airfield explanations of illusions and marsh gas and whatever they offer are definitely
a cover-up for the fact that there are some kind of object up there.
What the objects are, I'm not prepared to say.
I give you my opinion. My opinion is that the likelihood, the strongest possibility I can think of, of all the theories I've seen, is that they are simply people from outer space.
That becomes the most logical one to me.
For the simple reason that having been in the science end of this whole space field for many, many years, and having only been interested in UFOs, let's say, for the last year and a half,
to tie in and that astronomers and scientists all over the world now admit that there are millions
of civilized worlds throughout the universe that is the probability is very very high
the next step is to assume that many of these civilizations and and this they also uh admit
are many many uh thousands of years older than us and ours and uh technology is very great and
and there is no reason to suppose that they don't have ships here.
In other words, it becomes a negative way of looking at it.
But logically, with millions of worlds on base, that's the science end of it.
And the scientist doesn't dare go further except in private.
A lot of them in private do.
Now, what is your profession?
A science writer.
You're a science writer.
Yeah.
What magazine was that again?
Base World.
I edited it for quite a few years and had about two dozen books published.
Is there anything you're working on recently now?
that anybody can pick up?
Yes, in the science.
I have articles in Space World magazine
and, oh, there's one coming up in Mechanics Illustrated.
I can't keep track of which ones now are coming up.
And one of the men's magazines is called Gem.
That's about UFOs, incidentally.
In what, Rio magazine?
No, not in Rio.
I will have something, in fact, science articles
as well as you have articles in National Enquirer.
That's a tabloid thing, you know.
I notice you have a lot of these pictures on display that you were selling tonight.
Yeah, those are the originals of my syndicated panel,
which appears in about 100 papers.
About 60 in American and 40 foreign.
It appears daily, six days a week, and it started in the 1960s.
It's been going on all this time.
Could I see this now?
I want them to see these.
The nearest one in this area, the big New York papers don't have it.
The nearest one in this area is Patterson, New Jersey.
Patterson, New Jersey.
Yeah.
The Morning Call or something like that?
Patterson Evening News.
Patterson Evening News.
And they're...
Are these for sale today?
The originals are, yes, sir.
Where would we be able to purchase these other than here today?
Well, Jim Mosley will have them advertised on Saucer News,
and they can be ordered by mail from him eventually when he gets the ad in.
I don't know which issue it would be.
Most of these, as a matter of fact, are exclusive.
People write in to me, and they have never reported these before usually.
Or if they've reported to the Air Force, they've got the usual runaround.
And the first time they've been publicized in any way is in my column here.
I get hundreds and hundreds of letters from all these people, very sincere people.
No kooks, or very few kooks, here and there you can find them.
But these people are genuinely sincere about the fact that they've seen something,
and they describe it in great detail. They're very pleasant, usually.
And they're often in their letters saying,
What is it, Mr. Bender, as though I'm supposed to know?
And of course all I can write back is saying, I wish I knew.
But they're genuinely concerned, and they know they've seen something real.
Many of them are engineers, technical people who can't be fooled by balloons or helicopters
or anything like that, you know, on the main orbit.
Everything like that they've seen for many, many years.
Have you ever given any lectures yourself on these UFOs?
I've given short lectures.
I'm really not that well versed yet in the UFO field.
I'm still doing a lot of research.
Well, thank you very much for your time.
